newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa cellphone industry signs over 1 mln users.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa cellphone industry signs over 1 mln users.

text.p: South Africa's cellular telephone industry on Tuesday surpassed one million subscribers and is still poised for further growth, network operator Vodacom said.
"South Africa's cellular industry, barely three years old, passed the one million subscriber mark today," Vodacom managing director Alan Knott-Craig said in a statement.

He said that Vodacom -- 31.5 percent owned by Vodafone Group Plc -- had swelled its subscriber base to 606,000 subscribers on Tuesday and recently published statistics showed it had a 60 percent South African market share.

"(This) brings the total of subscribers to one million," Knott-Craig said. Rival operator Mobile Telephone Networks (MTN) has a subscriber base of 400,000, he said. MTN is jointly owned by Cable and Wireless Plc and local interest groups, including M-Cell Ltd.
The cellular network industry, which was launched on July 1, 1994 has recorded one of the fastest growth rates in the world.
Knott-Craig said Vodacom was budgeting for a million subscribers by the end of the year and the industry would reach a total of two million subscribers by the end of 1998.
Many outlying towns had been connected to the network and Vodacom was adding network capacity in metropolitan areas.
"One of the key factors of Vodacom's success has been the solid performance of our service providers who have provided the market reach required for such fast growth," he said.
